title: ALMA 0.1-0.2 arcsec Resolution Imaging of the NGC 1068 Nucleus: Compact Dense Molecular Gas Emission at the Putative AGN Location
question: Can compact dense molecular gas emission (HCN and HCO+ J=3-2) from the putative dusty torus at the AGN location in NGC 1068 be separated from the brighter eastern and western knots at 0.1-0.2 arcsec resolution, and what are its properties?

what.value: Clumpy torus model: torus outer size 20 (+6/-10) pc and gas mass (2.1±1.2)e5 Msun

evidence.loc: 4.1 Molecular emission from the putative AGN dusty torus
4.3 Molecular emission at the nuclear region
evidence.quote: central AGN luminosity of L$_{\rm AGN}$ $\sim$ 6 $\times$ 10$^{44}$ \[erg s$^{-1}$\]

recipe.method: uvcontsub with constant continuum, then clean with natural weighting; mfs for continuum
key_parameters: gain 0.1, threshold 0.8 mJy, 40 channels binned, 0.03 arcsec pixel

recipe.goal: Moment maps and spectral Gaussian fits
recipe.method: Moment 0 and 1 maps; Gaussian fits to spectra at E-peak, W-subpeak, C-peak and 2.4 arcsec radius region

recipe.goal: Torus size and dense gas mass
recipe.method: imfit for deconvolved size; HCN J=3-2 to J=1-0 luminosity assuming thermalized optically thick; M_dense=10 x L'HCN(1-0)
assumptions: HCN thermalized to J=3 and optically thick; conversion factor 10 Msun/(K km/s pc^2)

recipe.goal: Star formation estimate in SW region
recipe.method: Continuum flux in rectangle assuming solely free-free emission, converted to FIR luminosity and SFR

evidence.quote: The peak flux is estimated to be 9.2 mJy beam$^{-1}$ (51$\sigma$)
